vulnerability_type: Uncontrolled resource consumption via an unbounded reassembly buffer
summary: The CTAP HID vendor session appends payload chunks to a Vec with no size or count limit, and the caller only resets the session when the host declares the transfer finished, so a host that always sets more_data exhausts the device heap.
explanation: read_from_wire performs self.data.append(&mut w.data.clone()) with no bound, and fido2.rs:64 resets the session only on Ok(None) or Err. A host that keeps more_data true keeps finished false, so the handler returns the continue response and the buffer is retained across iterations. The ordering check at vendor_commands.rs:54 that might have terminated a malformed stream is inert because self.index is never assigned and stays zero, making the first conjunct always false. All of this runs before the allow_host consent gate, which in this build is permanently false since no store to it exists in the tree.
malicious_actor: malicious or compromised USB host to which the badge is attached
parameter: CTAP HID vendor command payload, more_data flag in the backup::Wire CBOR record
trigger_flow: USB HID vendor frame -> HidIterType::Vendor -> handle_vendor_data -> read_from_wire -> self.data.append with more_data set -> repeated without limit -> heap exhaustion -> process termination
malicious_input_example: a loop of CTAP HID vendor commands with command byte 0x71 carrying a CBOR backup::Wire record whose more_data field is always true and whose data field is full size
